```{python}
def box_extreme(resp, levels, mode="min", n=11, passes=4):
    """Extreme of the fitted surface over the WHOLE box, not only over its corners.

    The quadratic models carry curvature, so the minimum of a response over a factor
    box can lie inside the box. Successively refined grids on the same D.predict call.
    """
    lo = np.array([min(levels[f]) for f in FACT], dtype=float)
    hi = np.array([max(levels[f]) for f in FACT], dtype=float)
    a, b, best = lo.copy(), hi.copy(), None
    for _ in range(passes):
        mesh = np.meshgrid(*[np.linspace(a[i], b[i], n) for i in range(n_fact)],
                           indexing="ij")
        flat = {f: m.ravel() for f, m in zip(FACT, mesh)}
        v = np.asarray(D.predict(UO, resp, natural=flat), dtype=float)
        j = int(np.argmin(v)) if mode == "min" else int(np.argmax(v))
        best = (float(v[j]), {f: float(flat[f][j]) for f in FACT})
        c = np.array([flat[f][j] for f in FACT])
        h = (b - a) / (n - 1)
        a, b = np.maximum(lo, c - h), np.minimum(hi, c + h)
    return best
```

# Executive summary {.unnumbered}

Anion exchange chromatography is the final chromatographic step in the A-Mab drug substance
process. It is operated in flow-through mode, so the antibody passes through the column while
host cell protein, DNA, leached Protein A and virus bind to the resin. This report presents the
characterization of the step against its approved plan (PCP-008), executed on a qualified
scale-down model at commercial equivalent conditions. The work follows the lifecycle approach to
process validation [@fda2011] and the enhanced development approach of ICH Q8 and ICH Q11
[@ichq8; @ichq11], and the viral clearance evaluation follows ICH Q5A(R2) [@ichq5a]. The process
model, the criticality framework and the modular clearance approach are taken from the A-Mab
case study [@amab2009].

`{python} f"{n_par}"` process parameters were carried into the characterization,
`{python} f"{n_mv}"` of them in a multivariate design and `{python} f"{n_uv}"` univariately. All
of them are classified as well controlled critical process parameters. The step has no critical
process parameter and no key process parameter. The designed experiments were a screening study
of `{python} f"{n_scr}"` runs and a face-centred response-surface study of `{python} f"{n_rsm}"`
runs, both executed on the same scale-down column.

The critical quality attribute assigned to this step is the clearance of minute virus of mice
(MVM), which the drug substance register rates of very high criticality. The step also governs
pool host cell protein and contributes to the clearance of xenotropic murine leukaemia virus
(XMuLV). Response-surface models for these three responses are significant, and lack of fit is
not significant against the pure error of the centre-point replicates, so they are the
predictive basis of the design space. Step yield gave no significant model in either design, and
it did not respond to any of the `{python} f"{n_fact}"` factors over the ranges studied.

Every governed attribute meets its acceptance criterion everywhere in the characterized region.
The worst case for viral clearance lies at the low edge of load pH and the high edge of load
conductivity, with the other two parameters inside their ranges. There the fitted model predicts
an MVM log reduction factor of `{python} f"{mvm_worst:.2f}"` against a step requirement of
`{python} f"{acc_mvm_lo:.2f}"` log10, a margin of about `{python} f"{mvm_worst_margin_sd:.1f}"`
residual standard deviations of the model. The normal operating range sits well inside that
region, and the lowest MVM log reduction factor predicted anywhere inside it is
`{python} f"{mvm_nor_worst:.2f}"`.

Commercial-scale capability was estimated by Monte-Carlo simulation of `{python} f"{n_mc:,}"`
batches with every parameter varying inside its normal operating range. The cumulative MVM
clearance has a one-sided Cpk of `{python} f"{cpk_mvm:.2f}"`, with a mean of
`{python} f"{mean_mvm_cap:.2f}"` log10 against a requirement of `{python} f"{mvm_req:g}"` log10,
which is the tightest capability of any A-Mab drug substance attribute. Pool host cell protein
is far less constrained, with a Cpk of `{python} f"{cpk_hcp:.1f}"` against a limit of
`{python} f"{acc_hcp_hi:g}"` ng/mg.

`{python} f"{n_dev}"` deviations were recorded, and each was investigated, impact assessed and
closed (§13). One of them invalidated the first execution of both designs. The load material
used in that execution had an out of trend acidic charge variant content, the designs were
re-executed in full on a requalified load, and the analysis reported here is the re-executed
one. The other two were resolved without change to the fitted effects, to the operating region
or to the parameter classifications.

This step does not deliver the MVM requirement on its own. Small virus retentive filtration
(PCR-009) contributes the larger single increment to the cumulative claim, and the two
mechanisms are independent of each other. No claim is made here for the glycan or charge variant
attributes, which are formed at the production bioreactor (PCR-003) and are not modified by
anion exchange under platform conditions. The outcome of this report rolls up into the master
report (PCMR-001).

{{< pagebreak >}}

# Introduction

## Product and unit operation

A-Mab is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody produced in a fed-batch mammalian cell culture and
purified by a platform train of chromatographic and filtration steps. The train runs from
Protein A capture through low-pH viral inactivation, cation exchange, anion exchange and small
virus retentive filtration to ultrafiltration and diafiltration. Each step in the train has an
assigned role in the control strategy, and the roles are set out in the master plan (PCMP-001).
Anion exchange chromatography is Step 8 and the last chromatographic operation before the virus
filter.

The step is operated in flow-through mode. The column is equilibrated and washed at low
conductivity, the cation exchange eluate is titrated to the load pH and conductivity, and the
antibody passes through the resin while acidic impurities bind, because under these conditions
A-Mab carries a small net positive charge and does not bind. Host cell protein, DNA, leached
Protein A and virus particles carry a net negative charge and are retained. The pool is
collected across the load and the chase wash, and the column is then stripped and sanitized
under its life-cycle procedure (SOP-2008).

Two things follow from that mechanism, and both shape this study. The separation depends on the
difference in net charge between the product and the impurities, so it is governed by pH and by
ionic strength and not by the elution conditions that govern a bind and elute step. The step
also has no elution peak to cut, so the pool composition is set by how far collection runs into
the trailing edge of the flow-through peak. The step is credited with clearance of minute virus
of mice (a non-enveloped parvovirus), which is the hardest of the model viruses to remove. It is
also credited with clearance of xenotropic murine leukaemia virus and with a further reduction
of host cell protein, DNA and leached Protein A.

## Objectives

The objectives of the characterization were as follows.

(i) Quantify the relationship between the process parameters of the step and the quality
attributes and performance attributes it governs, over ranges wider than the intended operating
ranges.

(ii) Define a multivariate operating region in which the governed attributes remain within
their acceptance criteria.

(iii) Establish proven acceptable ranges for each parameter against each attribute it governs,
and confirm that the normal operating ranges sit inside them.

(iv) Classify each process parameter according to the decision logic of SOP-4001, using the
demonstrated effects and the capability with which the parameter can be controlled.

(v) Provide the justification for the Stage 2 ranges and for this step's contribution to the
overall control strategy, for consolidation in the master report (PCMR-001).

## Regulatory and scientific basis

The characterization is Stage 1 process design work in the sense of the lifecycle approach to
process validation [@fda2011]. It follows the enhanced development approach of ICH Q8 and ICH
Q11 [@ichq8; @ichq11], in which process understanding is built from prior knowledge and risk
assessment and is then bounded by designed experiments. Criticality is treated as a continuum in
the sense of ICH Q9 [@ichq9], so an attribute is placed on a scale from very low to very high
and the attributes of high and very high criticality are called critical. The same treatment is
applied to parameters through the classification in §9.

The viral clearance work follows ICH Q5A(R2) [@ichq5a]. Clearance is evaluated as a modular
claim: each contributing step is studied independently on a qualified small-scale spiking model,
and the increments are summed only where the mechanisms are independent. The A-Mab case study
[@amab2009] is the source of the process description, the quality attribute register and the
risk methodology used here.

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis

## Platform and prior-product knowledge

The anion exchange polishing step is a platform operation at Novacyte Biologics, used in the
manufacture of three previously licensed humanized IgG1 antibodies (X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab) and
in the supply of A-Mab clinical material. The resin, the buffer system and the mode of operation
have not changed across those products. The accumulated experience shows that the step is robust
in the sense that it delivers high yield and consistent impurity clearance when the load is
presented at the platform pH and conductivity. That experience reduces the amount of
optimization the A-Mab process required, and it sets the mechanistic expectations this study was
designed to confirm or refute.

Four expectations were carried into the design. Raising the load pH increases the net negative
charge on host cell protein and on the viral capsid, so it should increase both impurity binding
and virus retention, and raising the conductivity of the load screens those same charges, so it
should reduce clearance. The conductivity of the equilibration and wash-1 buffer sets the ionic
environment in which weakly bound species are either retained or displaced during the chase, so
it was expected to act mainly on pool host cell protein and only weakly on virus. Protein load
determines how much of the resin capacity is used, so it was expected to matter only if the
capacity for impurity binding were approached.

Prior knowledge also sets the boundaries of what this step is expected to do. Glycosylation
variants are not separated by charge-based chromatography, except for sialylated structures,
which are present in A-Mab at very low levels [@amab2009]. Charge variants are not modified by
the step, since the operation is a flow-through polish at fixed pH and the product does not
bind. Aggregate is reduced principally at the cation exchange step (PCR-007). None of these
attributes was measured as a response here, and none is claimed for this step.

## Quality attributes in scope

The step is assigned one critical quality attribute of its own, the clearance of minute virus of
mice, which the register rates of very high criticality.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cqas_for(UO))
```

: Critical quality attribute assigned to the anion exchange step. {#tbl-cqa-set}

The criticality in @tbl-cqa-set is the Tool #1 score of the A-Mab framework, which combines the
severity of the impact on the patient with the uncertainty in that assessment [@amab2009].
Attributes scored high or very high are treated as critical. Viral safety scores at the top of
the scale because the consequence of a failure is severe and because clearance cannot be
verified by testing the drug substance. The acceptance criterion in @tbl-cqa-set is a cumulative
requirement across the whole process, and the contribution required of this step is derived from
it in §7.

The step also governs, or contributes to, four further attributes that are set or formed
elsewhere in the process. They are listed below with the MVM row repeated from @tbl-cqa-set, so
that every attribute the step acts on appears in one place.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cqas_by_keys(["hcp", "residual_dna", "leached_protein_a", "lrv_xmulv", "lrv_mvm"]))
```

: Quality attributes the anion exchange step controls or clears. {#tbl-cqa-scope}

Host cell protein and the two viral clearance attributes were measured as responses of the
designed experiments, and residual DNA and leached Protein A were not. Both of the latter are
cleared to well inside their limits before this step, principally at Protein A capture (PCR-005)
and cation exchange (PCR-007), and both are measured in the anion exchange pool by validated
methods (AMV-3014 and AMV-3016), with their drug substance capability reported in §8 alongside
the rest. Making them responses of the design would have added two assays without adding process
understanding, because neither is close to its limit at the entry to this step.

## Risk-based prioritization and parameter selection

The scope of this study was set by the pre-characterization risk assessment (RA-001), which
ranked every parameter of the step on its potential impact on a critical quality attribute and
on its potential to interact with other parameters. Parameters were then sorted into those
warranting a multivariate study, those whose ranges could be supported by a univariate
assessment, and those requiring no new work because prior knowledge already bounds them.

`{python} f"{n_mv}"` parameters were assigned to the multivariate design. Load pH and load
conductivity were assigned because they set the charge difference the separation depends on, and
because the risk assessment expected them to interact. Equilibration and wash-1 conductivity was
assigned because it acts on the same binding equilibria at a different point in the cycle.
Protein load was assigned because a capacity limit, if one exists inside the studied range,
would show up as an interaction with conductivity and not as a main effect. Operating flow rate
was assigned to a univariate assessment, because it acts on residence time and not on the ion
exchange equilibria that the other four parameters set, and prior platform work has not linked
it to a quality attribute at this step.

The characterization ranges are wider than the intended operating ranges by a factor of between
`{python} f"{ratio_lo:.1f}"` and `{python} f"{ratio_hi:.1f}"`. The widths were chosen so that
the study bounds the process instead of confirming a point, and so that the knowledge space
supports later movement within the design space. The upper edge of the load pH range was set
below the point at which the product itself begins to bind, and the lower edge of the load
conductivity range was set above the point at which the titrated cation exchange eluate becomes
difficult to prepare reproducibly at scale. Both bounds are properties of the platform and not
of A-Mab.

{{< pagebreak >}}

# Materials and methods

## Scale-down model and its qualification

The studies were executed on a laboratory-scale column qualified as a model of the commercial
step under SOP-1001. The model uses the same resin, the same bed height and the same linear
velocity as the commercial column, and the load, wash and chase volumes are normalized to column
volumes. Protein load is expressed in grams of antibody per litre of resin, so it transfers
between scales directly. Buffer compositions are identical to the commercial buffers, and the
buffers used in the studies were released against the same specifications.

The qualification compared the scale-down model with commercial-scale data on the attributes
that enter and leave the step. Pool host cell protein, residual DNA, leached Protein A, step
yield and pool conductivity were compared at the target condition, and the column was compared
on plate count and peak asymmetry before each study. The model is judged qualified because no
difference between scales was found on those attributes that exceeded the reproducibility of the
methods. The qualification record is held with the study documentation for PCP-008 and is
summarized in the master plan (PCMP-001).

The viral clearance work used the same column operated as a small-scale spiking model in the
sense of ICH Q5A(R2) [@ichq5a]. The load was spiked with XMuLV or MVM to a titre high enough
that the log reduction factor can be measured against the assay limit of quantitation, and the
spiked material was clarified before loading so that the spike did not change the pressure
behaviour of the column. Spiking runs are performed in a containment laboratory and cannot be
run at commercial scale, so the clearance claim rests on the qualification of the model rather
than on at-scale confirmation. This is the principal limitation of the viral clearance claim and
it is stated again in §11.

The centre-point replicates of both designs are the pure error term used to test lack of fit in
§5, which is the second purpose of the qualification. Their spread is reported in §5.1 and it
sets the resolution of every effect estimate in this report.

## Operation

The step was operated as it is operated at commercial scale, under SOP-2011. The column is
sanitized and equilibrated with the equilibration buffer, whose conductivity is one of the
studied parameters. The cation exchange eluate is titrated to the load pH and adjusted to the
load conductivity, filtered and loaded at the operating flow rate. The load is followed by a
chase wash with the same buffer used for equilibration, which is the reason the buffer is
described here as the equilibration and wash-1 buffer. The flow-through pool is collected from
the start of the product breakthrough on the ascending edge of the UV trace until the trailing
edge falls to the collection set-point. The column is then stripped, sanitized and stored under
SOP-2008.

Several inputs to the step are controlled to platform specifications and were not varied. The
resin lot, the buffer compositions, the load filter, the column dimensions and the sanitization
regime are identity and quality controlled, not characterized, and the temperature of the
operation is held at ambient room conditions at both scales. The one input attribute that proved
to matter is the charge variant content of the cation exchange eluate, which is a property of
the upstream step and not a parameter of this one. It is discussed in §13.1 and it is the reason
a feed input control is proposed in §10.

## Analytical methods

Every response was measured by a validated method. The controlled documents that govern the step
and its assays are listed in @tbl-sops.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(sop_table(sops=AEX_SOP_REFS, amvs=AEX_AMV_REFS))
```

: Controlled documents governing the anion exchange characterization. {#tbl-sops}

Pool host cell protein was measured by the process-specific ELISA (AMV-3012) and is reported in
nanograms per milligram of antibody. XMuLV and MVM titres were measured by infectivity assay
(AMV-3017 and AMV-3018), and the log reduction factor is the difference between the log10 virus
load applied to the column and the log10 virus recovered in the pool, corrected for volume. Step
yield was determined from the antibody mass in the pool relative to the mass loaded, by
ultraviolet absorbance. Residual DNA and leached Protein A were measured in the pool by AMV-3014
and AMV-3016 respectively. The charge variant content of the load material was measured by
imaged capillary isoelectric focusing (AMV-3013), which is the method that detected the
deviation described in §13.1. Validated performance for these methods is summarized in Appendix
D.

## Sampling plan

Each design run produced a load sample, a flow-through pool sample and a strip sample. The load
sample establishes the input attributes and, for the spiking runs, the input virus titre. The
pool sample carries the responses. The strip sample was retained but was tested only where a
mass balance was needed to close an investigation. Every run in both designs was executed as a
spiking run, so a log reduction factor is reported for each of the `{python} f"{n_scr}"`
screening conditions and each of the `{python} f"{n_rsm}"` response-surface conditions.

The screening design carries `{python} f"{cp_scr}"` centre-point replicates and the
response-surface design carries `{python} f"{cp_rsm}"`. They were distributed through the run
order and not grouped, so that a drift in the assays or in the feed would show up as variation
between replicates, and run order within each design was randomized under SOP-1002.

## Statistical methods

The factors were coded so that the midpoint of the characterization range is zero and the two
edges are minus one and plus one, so effects are expressed per half-range, which makes factors
with different units comparable. The screening data were fitted by ordinary least squares with
all main effects and all two-factor interactions, and an effect is reported as twice the coded
coefficient, which is the change in the response across the full studied range of that factor.
The response-surface data were fitted with the full quadratic model in the same
`{python} f"{n_fact}"` factors, including the two-factor interactions and the squared terms.

A term is called significant at a significance level of 0.05, and model adequacy is judged on
four quantities together: the coefficient of determination, the adjusted value that penalises
added terms, the predicted value computed from the PRESS statistic, and the overall model F
test. Lack of fit was tested by partitioning the residual sum of squares into a lack of fit
component and a pure error component estimated from the centre-point replicates, and a model
whose lack of fit is not significant is treated as an adequate description of the surface. A
factor with no significant term in either design is called robust over the studied range, and
that conclusion is reported and not dropped.

Commercial-scale capability was estimated by Monte-Carlo simulation of `{python} f"{n_mc:,}"`
batches with every process parameter drawn inside its normal operating range. Capability is
reported as a one-sided Cpk against the acceptance criterion that applies to the attribute. No
numeric acceptance criterion for Cpk itself is defined for this campaign, so the capability
figures in §8 are read together with the margin between the simulated mean and the limit.

{{< pagebreak >}}

# Study design

## Factors, ranges and the knowledge space

The parameters carried into the study, their set-points, their normal operating ranges and their
characterization ranges are given in @tbl-params. The characterization range is the knowledge
space edge, which is the widest condition at which the step was run. It is not a proven
acceptable range, and the two are distinguished throughout this report.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(report_params(UO))
```

: Process parameters, ranges, study type and final classification. {#tbl-params}

The classification column in @tbl-params is the outcome of §9 and is shown here so that the
table is complete. The four multivariate factors are coded A to D throughout the report and the
appendices, using the legend in @tbl-legend.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.factor_legend_df(UO))
```

: Coded factor legend for the screening and response-surface designs. {#tbl-legend}

The centre point of both designs is the midpoint of each factor's characterization range, and it
was replicated so that the reproducibility of the step and of the assays could be estimated
independently of the model. Those replicates are the pure error term used in the lack of fit
tests.

## Screening design

The screening study was a two-level full factorial in the `{python} f"{n_fact}"` factors with
`{python} f"{cp_scr}"` centre points, giving `{python} f"{n_scr}"` runs. A full factorial was
chosen over a fractional design because the risk assessment (RA-001) expected interactions
between pH and the two conductivities, and a resolution IV fraction would have aliased those
interactions with each other. The design estimates every main effect and every two-factor
interaction without confounding.

The design is nonetheless near-saturated, spending most of its degrees of freedom on the model
and leaving few for residual error, so the residual is estimated from few degrees of freedom and
the adequacy statistics that depend on it are unstable (§5.2). The purpose of the screening
study is to identify which factors act on which response, and that is how its results are used
in §5.2. It is not the predictive model. The full coded design matrix and the measured responses
are given in Appendix A.

## Response-surface design

The response-surface study was a face-centred central composite design in the same
`{python} f"{n_fact}"` factors, with `{python} f"{cp_rsm}"` centre points and
`{python} f"{n_rsm}"` runs. The axial points sit on the faces of the cube rather than outside
it, so the design does not require the step to be run beyond the characterization ranges. Face
centring costs some rotatability and it is the right trade here, because the characterization
ranges were chosen as the limits of what the step should be asked to do.

All `{python} f"{n_fact}"` screening factors were carried into the response-surface design.
Reducing the factor set is the usual practice after a screening study, but two of the four
factors act on host cell protein and a different pair acts on the two viral responses, so
dropping either pair would have removed a governing factor for one of the governed attributes.
Protein load appears in neither pair, and it was retained so that the capacity question could be
bounded over the whole load range. Its absence of effect in the response-surface design is the
evidence that the resin capacity is not approached (§5.4). The design adds the curvature terms,
it is not near-saturated, and it supports interpolation inside the region. It is the predictive
model and the basis of the design space in §6, and its coded matrix and responses are in
Appendix B.

## Univariate assessment

Operating flow rate was assessed one factor at a time across its characterization range with the
other parameters at their set-points. It was excluded from the multivariate design for a
mechanistic reason. Flow rate changes the residence time of the load on the column, and the
binding of host cell protein and of virus to a strong anion exchanger under these conditions is
fast relative to the residence time at any flow rate in the studied range. It does not change
the charge difference that the separation depends on, so it cannot interact with pH or
conductivity in the way those three parameters interact with each other.

No effect estimate for flow rate on any governed attribute is reported in this document, and the
univariate runs are held in the study record for PCP-008. The classification of the parameter in
§9 therefore rests on its mechanism and on the control the skid applies to it under SOP-2011,
and not on a measured effect.

## Mechanistic interpretation

The results follow the mechanism the step was expected to work by, and the two governing pairs
separate for a physical reason. Virus clearance depends on the binding of the capsid to the
resin during the load, so it responds to the pH and the ionic strength of the load and to
nothing else in the studied set. Host cell protein clearance depends on the same binding
equilibria, but the species involved are a heterogeneous population with a wide range of
isoelectric points, and the weakly bound part of that population is displaced during the chase
wash. That is why host cell protein responds to the conductivity of the equilibration and wash-1
buffer while virus does not.

The interaction between load pH and wash-1 conductivity has the same explanation. At low wash
conductivity the weakly bound host cell protein species stay on the column whatever the load pH
was, so the pH effect is muted. At high wash conductivity those species are displaced into the
pool, and the load pH then decides how strongly they were bound in the first place. The
consequence for control is direct: the two parameters must be considered together, and a proven
acceptable range for either one that ignores the other would misstate the risk.

The absence of a protein load effect on any response is the most useful negative result of the
study. If the resin capacity for impurity binding were being approached at the top of the load
range, the clearance responses would fall and the effect would appear as an interaction between
load and conductivity. No such term is significant in either design. The step therefore has
capacity margin across the whole studied load range, and the load can be used as an operational
lever without a quality consequence. The one caveat is that the studied range is bounded, and
this study says nothing about loads above its upper edge.

Step yield is high and flat because the product does not bind. In a flow-through operation the
only routes to product loss are non-specific interaction with the resin and incomplete recovery
of the pool, and neither is sensitive to the parameters studied here over these ranges. The
predicted yield at the set-point is `{python} f"{yield_sp:.3f}"`, which is consistent with the
centre-point mean of `{python} f"{mean_yield_cp:.3f}"`.

{{< pagebreak >}}

# Design space

The design space for this step is the whole characterized region in the `{python} f"{n_fact}"`
multivariate parameters. Every governed attribute is predicted to meet its acceptance criterion
everywhere in that region, so the region is not cut back by any attribute inside the ranges
studied. This is a stronger result than the study was designed to produce.

The region has two principal planes. Viral clearance is governed by load pH and load
conductivity, and host cell protein by load pH and the equilibration and wash-1 conductivity
(§5.4). Load pH appears in both, which makes it the parameter that ties the region together.
Protein load appears in neither, so it enters the region only as the range over which the other
three were studied.

The worst case for the region is not one of its corners. The MVM model carries positive squared
terms in the equilibration and wash-1 conductivity and in the protein load (@tbl-coef-mvm), so
its lowest predicted value lies inside the region and not at a vertex, and the region was
searched on a refined grid. Neither squared term is significant on its own, and the search was
made over the fitted model as it stands. The worst point sits at load pH
`{python} natstr(mvm_worst_at, 'load_ph')`, equilibration and wash-1 conductivity
`{python} natstr(mvm_worst_at, 'wash1_cond')` mS/cm, load conductivity
`{python} natstr(mvm_worst_at, 'load_cond')` mS/cm and protein load
`{python} natstr(mvm_worst_at, 'load')` g/L resin. There the model predicts an MVM log
reduction factor of `{python} f"{mvm_worst:.2f}"` against the step requirement of
`{python} f"{acc_mvm_lo:.2f}"` log10 derived in §7, and an XMuLV log reduction factor of
`{python} f"{xmulv_worst:.2f}"` against `{python} f"{acc_xmulv_lo:.2f}"` log10. The MVM margin
there is `{python} f"{mvm_worst_margin:.2f}"` log10, which is about
`{python} f"{mvm_worst_margin_sd:.1f}"` times the residual standard deviation of the fitted
model (`{python} f"{rmse_mvm:.2f}"` log10). The worst case for host cell protein is at a
different point, where the model predicts `{python} f"{hcp_worst:.1f}"` ng/mg against a limit of
`{python} f"{acc_hcp_hi:g}"` ng/mg.

The normal operating ranges sit inside the characterized region with room to spare. Searching
the normal operating box the same way, the lowest predicted MVM log reduction factor is
`{python} f"{mvm_nor_worst:.2f}"`, a margin of `{python} f"{mvm_nor_margin:.2f}"` log10 or
about `{python} f"{mvm_nor_margin_sd:.1f}"` residual standard deviations. The lowest predicted
XMuLV log reduction factor in the same box is `{python} f"{xmulv_nor_worst:.2f}"` and the
highest predicted pool host cell protein is `{python} f"{hcp_nor_worst:.1f}"` ng/mg. The nesting
is the conventional one: the normal operating range lies inside the design space, which lies
inside the knowledge space bounded by the characterization ranges [@amab2009].

Three bounds apply to this claim and none of them is removable by more analysis of these data.
The models predict mean levels, so at the edge of the region the reliability of an individual
batch is lower than the mean statement suggests, and the margin at the worst case is smaller
than the model's own residual standard deviation. The claim covers the four parameters that were
varied, at the ranges in @tbl-params, with the load presented at the charge variant content of a
representative cation exchange eluate. It rests on a qualified scale-down
model and, for the viral responses, on a small-scale spiking model that cannot be run at
commercial scale (§3.1).

Movement within the design space is not a regulatory change in the sense of ICH Q8 [@ichq8],
although it remains subject to the pharmaceutical quality system and to a prospective assessment
of the particular move [@ichq10]. Movement outside it requires change control and, for a
parameter that governs viral clearance, a new assessment of the modular claim.

{{< pagebreak >}}

# Proven acceptable ranges

The design space in §6 is a multivariate region, and it is complemented here by proven
acceptable ranges, which are per attribute and per parameter, because a control strategy has to
be written in terms a batch record can carry.

The acceptance basis differs by attribute. For pool host cell protein the criterion is the drug
substance specification, an upper limit of `{python} f"{acc_hcp_hi:g}"` ng/mg. For the two viral
attributes the drug substance criterion is a cumulative log reduction across the process, so the
criterion that applies to this step is the required step contribution, obtained by subtracting
the clearance credited to the other steps from the cumulative requirement. For MVM the
cumulative requirement is `{python} f"{mvm_req:g}"` log10, the other credited steps contribute
`{python} f"{other_mvm:.2f}"` log10, and the requirement on this step is therefore
`{python} f"{acc_mvm_lo:.2f}"` log10. For XMuLV the same calculation gives
`{python} f"{acc_xmulv_lo:.2f}"` log10, and these step level criteria are used throughout this
section and in §6.

Two analyses were run for each attribute and parameter pair. The first holds the other
parameters at their set-points and evaluates the fitted response-surface model across the
parameter's characterization range. The second propagates the normal operating ranges of the
other parameters: they are drawn by Monte-Carlo inside their normal operating ranges, the fitted
model is evaluated with the model's residual variation added, and the parameter is acceptable
where the whole 95 percent predictive interval stays within the criterion. The second analysis
is a robustness criterion, so it is the narrower of the two by construction. Both are reported
in @tbl-par.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.par_table(UO))
```

: Proven acceptable ranges per governed attribute and parameter, from both analyses. {#tbl-par}

For every attribute and every parameter the two analyses agree, and both span the full
characterization range. No parameter has a sub-range within which the governed attribute fails,
and no parameter loses acceptable range when the other three are allowed to vary within their
normal operating ranges. The MVM rows are the ones to read first, because MVM carries the
tightest requirement of the three attributes, and even there the acceptable range for load pH
runs from the bottom to the top of the studied range.

That outcome has a consequence for how the ranges should be used. Since no univariate proven
acceptable range is binding, the constraint on the operating region is the multivariate worst
case identified in §6 and not any single parameter limit in @tbl-par. A batch record that held
each parameter inside its row of @tbl-par independently would not be relying on a proven
constraint, because the rows were computed with the other parameters at their set-points or
inside their normal operating ranges, not at their own extremes.

The representative plots follow, one per governed attribute, each against the parameter with the
largest main effect on it. In each figure the acceptance limit is drawn, the acceptable region
is shaded green, and the set-point and normal operating range are marked, with the left panel
giving the first analysis and the right panel the second.


These ranges are bounded by the characterization ranges and by the fitted models, so they are
not evidence about conditions outside @tbl-params, and they carry the assumptions of §6 on the
scale-down model and on the charge variant content of the load.

{{< pagebreak >}}

# Parameter classification

Every parameter of the step is classified well controlled critical process parameter, and no
parameter is classified critical process parameter. The distinction follows SOP-4001 and the
A-Mab decision logic: both classes cover parameters whose variability can affect a critical
quality attribute, and the difference is the risk of leaving the design space [@amab2009]. That
risk is low for every parameter here, because the design space extends to the full characterized
range and the normal operating ranges in @tbl-params sit inside it.

- Load pH is a well controlled critical process parameter with the largest main effect on both
viral responses and the second largest on host cell protein, and it appears in both governing
planes of the design space. It is classified well controlled rather than critical because the
titration is performed in a controlled vessel with an in-line measurement, and because the
acceptable range extends across the whole characterized range and does not stop inside it.

- Equilibration and wash-1 conductivity is a well controlled critical process parameter. It has
the largest main effect on pool host cell protein and it interacts with load pH. It is prepared
by buffer dilution and is verified on release, so an out of range value is detected before use,
which is what happened in the deviation described in §13.3.

- Load conductivity is a well controlled critical process parameter. It has the second largest
main effect on both viral responses and no resolved effect on host cell protein. It is set by
titration of the cation exchange eluate and is measured in line before loading.

- Protein load is a well controlled critical process parameter, although no effect of protein
load on any governed attribute was resolved in either design, which is evidence that the resin
capacity is not approached within the studied range. The classification is retained rather than
reduced because the parameter sets how much impurity is presented to a finite number of binding
sites, so its effect is bounded by the studied range and not by mechanism. It is easy to
control, since it is computed from the measured mass of the load.

- Operating flow rate is a well controlled critical process parameter. It was assessed
univariately, and this report presents no effect estimate for it (§4.4). The classification
rests on the mechanism, in that flow rate sets residence time, and on the control the skid
applies to the parameter under SOP-2011, over a normal operating range that lies inside the
range characterized (@tbl-params).

No parameter of this step is classified key process parameter or general process parameter,
which is a consequence of the step's role and not of the size of the effects. Every parameter of
a step that carries a viral clearance claim is linked to a critical quality attribute through
the clearance mechanism, even where the measured effect is small, and the counts across the
whole train are consolidated in PCMR-001.

{{< pagebreak >}}

# Contribution to the control strategy

The step contributes four elements to the control strategy, and it delivers none of them in
isolation.

The first is parameter control. The `{python} f"{n_par}"` parameters are held within the normal
operating ranges in @tbl-params, which sit inside the design space established in §6. The two
that carry the viral clearance claim, load pH and load conductivity, are set by titration of the
cation exchange eluate and are verified before the load begins.

The second is in-process monitoring. Pool host cell protein is measured on every batch by
AMV-3012 and trended, and residual DNA and leached Protein A are measured by AMV-3014 and
AMV-3016. Pool conductivity, pool pH and step yield are recorded as process attributes. The UV
trace of the flow-through peak is recorded, and the pool collection set-point on the trailing
edge is a fixed value in the batch record following the correction described in §13.2.

The third is the viral clearance claim itself, which is modular: this step is credited with
`{python} f"{aex_mvm:.2f}"` log10 of MVM clearance and `{python} f"{aex_xmulv:.2f}"` log10 of
XMuLV clearance. The claim is additive only because the mechanisms are independent: charge-based
partitioning here, size-based retention at the virus filter (PCR-009), and chemical inactivation
at low pH (PCR-006). Against MVM the low-pH step contributes nothing, so the cumulative claim of
`{python} f"{cum_mvm:.2f}"` log10 rests on this step and the virus filter together. The
consolidated claim is reported in PCMR-001.

The fourth is a feed input control that arises from a deviation, since the charge variant
content of the cation exchange eluate is an input attribute of this step, and an extended
neutralized hold of that eluate raised it enough to change the behaviour of the step (§13.1). A
hold time limit on the cation exchange eluate before anion exchange loading is therefore
proposed as part of the control strategy, and the icIEF method (AMV-3013) is available to verify
the input where a hold excursion occurs.

Life-cycle controls sit alongside these, in that resin re-use is limited and the column is
repacked and re-qualified under SOP-2008, with a qualification that includes the plate count and
asymmetry criteria used in this study. Resin life-cycle performance was not a factor of these
designs, and the clearance claim is made for a column within its validated re-use limit.

The step does not modify the glycan or charge variant attributes of the product, which are
formed at the bioreactor (PCR-003). It is not the principal aggregate polish, which is the
cation exchange step (PCR-007), and it does not by itself meet the cumulative viral clearance
requirement for either model virus.

{{< pagebreak >}}

# Discussion

The step is well understood at the end of this study, and the understanding is mechanistic
rather than empirical. Two parameters govern virus clearance, a partly different pair governs
host cell protein, and the reason for the split follows from the chemistry of a flow-through
anion exchanger (§5.4). The main effects are the effects the prior knowledge section expected,
and they act in the directions it expected. The interaction is the one expectation the study did
not meet. The risk assessment expected load pH and load conductivity to interact, and no such
term was resolved in either design, while the interaction that governs the step is between load
pH and the equilibration and wash-1 conductivity. The full factorial was still the right design,
because it could have resolved either.

The scale-down model is the foundation of every quantitative claim in this report, and its
representativeness is supported in two ways. The qualification compared input and output
attributes between scales and found no difference beyond method reproducibility (§3.1). The
centre-point replicates then reproduced within a few percent for every response except host cell
protein, where a fraction of `{python} f"{hcp_varfrac:g}"` of the variance is attributed to the
ELISA. Neither of those is a demonstration that the model predicts the commercial column at the
edges of the design space, and that limitation is general to Stage 1 work [@amab2009].

The first of the three deviations is genuinely adverse. The first execution of both designs used
a load whose acidic charge variant content was
`{python} f"{dev_008_01_acidic_variants_deamidated_pct:g}"` percent
against `{python} f"{dev_008_01_acidic_variants_requalified_pct:g}"` percent in the requalified
material, and at the high load and high wash conductivity corner it drove pool host cell protein
above the acceptance criterion applied to it. The designs were invalidated for operating region
definition and re-executed in full, the root cause is understood, the anomalous interaction is
absent from the requalified data, and the reported analysis uses only the requalified execution
(§13.1). The residual position is that this step is sensitive to an input attribute that was not
previously controlled, and the control strategy now carries a hold time limit for that reason.

Three limitations bound what the report claims. The viral clearance results come from a
small-scale spiking model that cannot be run at commercial scale, so the clearance claim is a
modular claim supported by a qualified model and not by at-scale measurement. The
response-surface models predict mean levels, and their predicted coefficients of determination,
the lowest being `{python} f"{predr2_gov_lo:.3f}"`, set the limit of what should be read from a
prediction at an untested condition. Resin life-cycle was not a variable of the study, so the
claims hold for a column within its validated re-use limit and the life-cycle evidence sits in
SOP-2008.

No parameter of this step required the most stringent control class. The reason is not that the
effects are small, because two of them are large, but that the acceptable region extends to the
edges of the characterization ranges and the parameters are held far inside it. A critical
process parameter designation would be appropriate if a design space edge fell inside the range
the equipment can reach, and no such edge was found here.

{{< pagebreak >}}

# Conclusions

The anion exchange step is characterized and its operating region is defined. The
`{python} f"{n_fact}"` multivariate parameters were studied over ranges between
`{python} f"{mv_ratio_lo:.1f}"` and `{python} f"{mv_ratio_hi:.1f}"` times the width of their
normal operating ranges, and response-surface models for pool host cell protein and for both
viral responses are adequate and free of significant lack of fit.

The design space is the full characterized region. Every governed attribute meets its acceptance
criterion everywhere in it, and the worst case is the MVM log reduction factor at
`{python} f"{mvm_worst:.2f}"` log10 against a step requirement of `{python} f"{acc_mvm_lo:.2f}"`
log10. The proven acceptable ranges span the full characterization range for every attribute and
parameter pair, under both analyses, so the binding constraint on the operating region is the
multivariate worst case and not a univariate limit.

At commercial scale the attributes this step governs meet their acceptance criteria, and the
tightest capability is the cumulative MVM clearance at a Cpk of `{python} f"{cpk_mvm:.2f}"` with
a mean of `{python} f"{mean_mvm_cap:.2f}"` log10 against `{python} f"{mvm_req:g}"` log10. All
`{python} f"{n_par}"` parameters are classified well controlled critical process parameters and
none is a critical process parameter.

`{python} f"{n_dev}"` deviations were recorded and closed. One invalidated the first execution
of both designs, which were re-executed in full, and none of the three changed a parameter
classification or the operating region. The clearance credited to this step is one increment of
a modular claim that also rests on small virus retentive filtration and, for enveloped virus, on
low-pH inactivation. Confirmation at commercial scale is a Stage 2 activity and has not been
performed, and these results roll up into the master report (PCMR-001).

{{< pagebreak >}}

approved. One of them invalidated the first execution of both designs and is described first.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(dev_register(DOC))
```

: Deviation register for the anion exchange characterization. {#tbl-dev}

@tbl-dev lists the three. The first has a disposition of invalidation and re-execution, which is
the most severe of the three dispositions and is treated at the greatest length below. The second was corrected by modelling and
verification runs and applies to both executions, and the third was retained, which means the
run was kept in the analysis with a documented justification.

## DEV-008-01: non-representative load in the first execution

The first execution of both designs produced pool host cell protein above the acceptance
criterion applied to it. The highest value in the first screening execution was
`{python} f"{sup_hcp_max:.0f}"` ng/mg against the criterion of `{python} f"{acc_hcp_hi:g}"`
ng/mg, and the highest in the first response-surface execution was
`{python} f"{sup_hcp_max_rsm:.0f}"` ng/mg. `{python} f"{n_sup_over}"` of the
`{python} f"{n_sup_runs}"` runs across the two first executions exceeded the criterion, and all
of them lay at or near the corner combining high protein load with high equilibration and wash-1
conductivity. In the re-executed designs reported here the highest pool host cell protein at any
condition is `{python} f"{req_hcp_max:.1f}"` ng/mg.

The investigation began from the load material, and charge variant analysis by icIEF (AMV-3013)
of the load used in the first execution, lot LOT-CEX-8842, returned an acidic variant content of
`{python} f"{dev_008_01_acidic_variants_deamidated_pct:g}"` percent against
`{python} f"{dev_008_01_acidic_variants_requalified_pct:g}"` percent for the requalified load.
The cation exchange eluate had been held after neutralization for
`{python} f"{dev_008_01_neutralized_hold_h:g}"` hours before titration, and the root cause was
assigned as asparagine deamidation promoted by that extended hold. Deamidation lowers the
isoelectric point of the affected species, which increases their affinity for an anion exchanger
at the load pH and puts them in competition with the host cell protein population for the same
binding sites.

The mechanism predicts a specific statistical signature, and the data carry it. In the first
execution protein load had a large effect on pool host cell protein and it interacted strongly
with the equilibration and wash-1 conductivity, and neither term survives in the requalified
data.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(sup_cmp("hcp_out_ng_mg", ["B", "D", "BD", "A"]))
```

: Screening effects on pool host cell protein in the first (invalidated) and requalified executions. {#tbl-sup-cmp}

@tbl-sup-cmp compares the four largest terms of the first execution with the same terms in the
requalified execution. The protein load effect falls from
`{python} f"{efs('hcp_out_ng_mg','D'):.1f}"` ng/mg (p `{python} pfmt(efsp('hcp_out_ng_mg','D'))`) to `{python} f"{ef('hcp_out_ng_mg','D'):.1f}"` ng/mg (p
`{python} pfmt(efp('hcp_out_ng_mg','D'))`), and the interaction between protein load and wash-1
conductivity falls from `{python} f"{efs('hcp_out_ng_mg','BD'):.1f}"` ng/mg (p
`{python} pfmt(efsp('hcp_out_ng_mg','BD'))`) to `{python} f"{ef('hcp_out_ng_mg','BD'):.1f}"`
ng/mg (p `{python} pfmt(efp('hcp_out_ng_mg','BD'))`). The wash-1 conductivity effect, which is
a property of the step rather than of the load, is present in both executions and changes only
in magnitude. Competition for a finite number of binding sites is exactly what produces a load
by conductivity interaction, and its disappearance when the competing species are removed
confirms the root cause.

The disposition was to invalidate both designs for the purpose of defining the operating region
and to re-execute them in full on a requalified, representative load. The re-executed datasets
are the ones analysed in §5 to §9 of this report, and the first execution is retained as a
superseded dataset, referenced here for root cause confirmation and not used for any
quantitative claim about the step. Its value is that it characterizes the behaviour of the step
when the load is not representative, which is information the control strategy uses (§10).

Two consequences follow. A hold time limit on the neutralized cation exchange eluate before
anion exchange loading is proposed as a feed input control. Where a hold excursion occurs, the
charge variant content of the load is to be verified by AMV-3013 before the step is run, because
the first execution shows that an out of trend load changes which parameters matter and not only
how well the step performs.

## DEV-008-02: pool collection set-point on the trailing edge

The pool collection set-point used on the trailing edge of the flow-through peak was more
permissive than the value the method now specifies. Both executions collected to
`{python} f"{dev_008_02_uv_pool_stop_original_mau:g}"` mAU, and the set-point was subsequently
corrected to `{python} f"{dev_008_02_uv_pool_stop_corrected_mau:g}"` mAU. The deviation was
found during the post-execution reconciliation of pool fractions against the host cell protein
results (AMV-3012), after both designs had been executed.

The impact is a common offset and not a distortion of the design. The same set-point was applied
to every run of both executions, so it shifts the intercept of every fitted model and leaves the
estimated factor effects unchanged. Pool host cell protein is the response affected, because it
is the response that depends on how far collection runs into the trailing edge. The viral
responses are computed from the ratio of virus in the load to virus in the pool, and both
quantities move with the pool volume, so the log reduction factor is far less sensitive to the
collection window.

The correction was evaluated by applying the fitted models at the corrected collection window
and confirmed with `{python} f"{dev_008_02_ver_n:g}"` verification runs, of which
`{python} f"{dev_008_02_ver_robust_n:g}"` were placed at the extremes of the operating region
and not at the centre. The verification set is small. With
`{python} f"{dev_008_02_ver_n:g}"` runs and the intermediate precision of the host cell protein
ELISA, the 95 percent confidence half-width on the verification mean is
`{python} f"{dev_008_02_ci_hw:g}"` percent of that mean. The verification therefore confirms
that the corrected set-point produces host cell protein of the same order as the models predict,
and it does not resolve a difference smaller than that half-width. That resolution is sufficient
here only because the margin to the limit is large, at a simulated mean of
`{python} f"{mean_hcp_cap:.1f}"` ng/mg against `{python} f"{acc_hcp_hi:g}"` ng/mg (§8). The
disposition is that the corrected set-point is fixed in the batch record and the reported
operating region is unchanged.

## DEV-008-03: equilibration and wash-1 buffer released below its pH range

One screening run was executed with an equilibration and wash-1 buffer that had been released
outside its pH acceptance range. Buffer lot LOT-BUF-8815 measured
`{python} f"{dev_008_03_buffer_ph_measured:g}"` against a lower acceptance limit of
`{python} f"{dev_008_03_buffer_ph_low_limit:g}"` and a target of
`{python} f"{dev_008_03_buffer_ph_target:g}"`. The deviation was found during buffer release
testing under SOP-2103, and the root cause was a titration endpoint error at buffer preparation.

The run was retained in the analysis. The buffer pH is not a factor of the design, but it sets
the pH of the column at the start of the load, so the excursion acts in the same direction as a
lower load pH. The measured value lies inside the load pH characterization range of
`{python} f"{CFG.unit_op(UO).param('load_ph').prange[0]:g}"` to
`{python} f"{CFG.unit_op(UO).param('load_ph').prange[1]:g}"`, near its lower edge, over which
the effect of pH on every response was quantified. The argument for retaining the run rests on
the direction of the bias. Lower pH reduces both viral clearance and host cell protein clearance,
which means the excursion biases the affected run towards worse apparent performance and cannot
flatter the result.

The effect on the fitted models is one run out of `{python} f"{n_scr}"`, at a shift smaller
than the half-range of the load pH factor, on a response whose centre-point coefficient of
variation is `{python} f"{cv_hcp_scr:.1f}"` percent. The disposition is retained without
adjustment, a corrective action was raised against the buffer preparation procedure, and the
release test that detected the excursion is unchanged and remains the detection control.

## Appendix A: screening design matrix and responses

The coded settings of the `{python} f"{n_scr}"` screening runs are in @tbl-appa-set and the
